title: Making A Large Island
description_md:
Given an `n x n` binary `grid`, you may change at most one `0` to a `1`. Return
the size of the largest island possible afterward (an island is a 4-directionally connected group of `1`s).

test_cases.explanation: The two 1's at (0,0) and (1,1) aren't connected -- they only touch diagonally, which doesn't count. Flipping the 0 at (0,1) works because it's adjacent to (0,0) in its row AND to (1,1) in its column, joining all three cells into a single island of size 3. (Flipping (1,0) instead gives the same result by symmetry.)
